messages:
sara: Heads up — canary on dedicated-5 shows host-side p95 spike (~60ms) for streaming tokenize requests after last runtime change. Repro steps below.

mike: saw it too. pprof shows user CPU hot in parse_tokenizer::tokenize and grpc::hpack::decode. HPACK table churn looks high.

sara: quick perf top sample: 'parse_tokenizer::tokenize 28.4% | grpc::hpack::decode 22.1% | http2::writev_flush 9.3%'. attaching a tiny flame (will push full to infra).

anya: interesting — did kernel-selection change in that build? we enabled avx2_small_seq hint last week which picked a different codepath for short sequences. config snippet from the canary: 
```
{"kernel_hint":"avx2_small_seq","batching":{"min_tokens":8,"max_latency_ms":5}}
```

tim: we have lots of tiny streaming chunks (1-5 tokens) from the chat client, so raising min_tokens or switching kernel might increase tiny-batch frequency and header pressure.

mike: KV-cache also shows regression: miss rate jumped 1.2% -> 6.8% on canary. recent kvcache checkpoint added a mutex in lookup hot path — that could amplify CPU when combined with header decode.

deploy-bot: build-5478 deployed to canary at 2634567890

sara: quick mitigation I tested locally: reuse tokenizer instance per connection (avoid per-chunk alloc/init) + pre-serialize common gRPC headers. p95 dropped ~20% on short flows. toggled TCP_CORK/writev coalesce on ingress; helped reduce syscall rate.

anya: can we do a streaming-special-case in batching: if streaming && seq_len <= 8, accumulate up to 16ms or up to 12 tokens before dispatch? avoids too many tiny batches but keeps latency.

tim: also think about HPACK: we should add static entries for common headers (content-type, authorization, x-client-id) so decoding cost drops. header table churn is expensive for short frames.

mike: i'll open a PR to remove the mutex in the KV lookup and replace with a seqlock/lock-free read path, but need to add perf-regression tests first.

sara: plan for next 24h: 1) rollback avx2_small_seq kernel hint on canary 2) land tokenizer reuse for connections 3) enable writev coalesce / TCP_CORK on ingress 4) KV lookup refactor in branch + perf harness. i'll run the e2e perf job tonight and post numbers.

anya: :thumbsup: please add an e2e perf job that drives 1-5 token streaming traces + header-heavy clients. tag me when PRs are up.

tim: small note — grpc hpack decoder currently allocates per-header; consider an inline small-buffer vector to avoid heap churn for <=4 headers.

sara: fyi logs from canary: increased 100-200 header frames/s and ~12% higher syscall rate on ingress. pushing full traces to /infra/prof/2634567890-flame.svg and a short perf summary in the ticket.

mike: :eyes: thanks. cc @eng-sre in case infra wants to tune net.core settings for writev coalescing while we iterate.

sara: will follow up with a short report after the perf run.
